citations.title: On the Optimality of Randomization in Experimental Design: How to Randomize for Minimax Variance and Design-Based Inference
citations.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society, Series B 83, 404--409
citations.statement: For the ellipsoidal conditional-mean class M_K = {K u : uᵀ K u ≤ C} with K ⪰ 0, a symmetric balanced mixed design σ with assignment second moment Q(σ) has worst-case design variance V(σ, M_K) = C · λ_max(K^{1/2} Q(σ) K^{1/2}), and the randomized mixed-strategy optimal design minimizes that largest-eigenvalue criterion over the paper's feasible design class.
citations.verbatim_statement: An example is M_K := {K u : u^T K u <= C} for a positive semidefinite K, for which V(sigma,M_K)=C lambda_max(K^(1/2) Q(sigma) K^(1/2)). The randomized MSOD solves min over sigma in S of this largest-eigenvalue criterion.

attestation.note: Verified 2026-08-08 against the publisher HTML for Kallus (2021), Section 5, opening paragraphs (journal pp. 407-408), https://academic.oup.com/jrsssb/article/83/2/404/7056002; the page states the ellipsoidal class and variance formula and then defines the randomized MSOD minimization over sigma in S.

lem:balanced-covariance-realizability.notes: `{A_d : d ∈ D_n} = C_n`, with the sign-symmetrization construction that turns any convex representation into a mean-zero attaining design. Build-inline (medium): forward inclusion is `convexHull` membership of a finite convex combination (`Finset.centerMass` / `mem_convexHull_iff_exists_fintype`); the converse builds an explicit `FiniteDesign` putting mass `a_j/2` on `±z^(j)` and verifies `p_nonneg`/`p_sum`, closure of the balanced set under sign reversal (needs `Even n`), zero mean, and covariance invariance under `z ↦ −z`. This lemma is the implementability bridge consumed by `thm:exact-oracle-saddle`, `thm:finite-unknown-quality-regret`, and `thm:exact-pair-space-regret`.

thm:cone-lift-dual.notes: Rank-one exactness of the lift, the scalar dual `q_ρ(A;S) = inf_{η ≥ 0}{λ_max(A + η P_S | H_n) − η ρ²}`, and the compactified attainment statement. Build-inline and IN SCOPE — every step is elementary and fully written out in the core's `proof_tex`; nothing here is open mathematics. It is, however, the heaviest single obligation, so it is planned as a theorem file over four dedicated helper files: `Helpers/ExtremePoints.lean` (extreme points of the compact convex `K_s` are rank one, via the trace-zero/score-trace-zero perturbation `D` supported on `range X` — over `Mathlib.Analysis.Convex.Extreme` + `KreinMilman`); `Helpers/Separation.lean` (the elementary compact BILINEAR minimax on `E_H × [0,K]` from finite-dimensional strong separation of the compact convex 2-D image set — Mathlib has NO convexity-based minimax, see the S2 search trace, so this is a small reusable build-inline helper, NOT a Defer item, since the core supplies the whole separation argument); `Helpers/Spectral.lean` (`max_{X ∈ E_H} tr((A + ηP_S)X) = λ_max(A + ηP_S | H_n)` and Rayleigh attainment); `Helpers/Compactness.lean` (the `Φ_K → primal` penalty limit and the `s = 1` endpoint estimate `u = x + y`, `≤ c + L_A²/(η − L_A)`). ANALOGOUS modules for F3: `EXP_SaturationSkewThreshold_Research/Helpers/{ExtremePoints,Duality}.lean` (same Krein–Milman + separation pattern for a saturation moment problem).

thm:exact-oracle-saddle.notes: The full-hull saddle identity `v* = min_{A ∈ C_n} max_{X ∈ X_ρ(S)} tr(AX) = max_X min_{z ∈ Z_n} zᵀXz`, its `(X,t)` program form, the attaining sign-pair design `d*_{ρ,S} ∈ D_n`, and the matching converse in SATE-risk units. (1)) proved by the projection/separation argument onto `ℝ_+^J` — factored into `Helpers/SimplexMinimax.lean` (reusing `Helpers/Separation.lean`); ANALOGOUS module `EXP_DesignPm1ExactnessBoundaryV1_Research/Helpers/WeightedSimplexKKT.lean` (the same simplex active-set/first-order optimality pattern over a weighted simplex). The design-side conversion is `lem:balanced-covariance-realizability`; the risk-side conversion is `lem:exact-design-risk` composed with the bijection `μ = √(nM)·u` between the shell and the score-constrained unit sphere. The `n = 4, S = H_n` smallest-case check is discharged in `Helpers/FourUnit.lean` and re-exported here.

thm:admissibility-frontier.notes: The headline: `(i) S ∈ 𝔄_n ⟺ (ii) κ(S) < c_n ⟺ (iii) γ(S) < 1`, `ρ*(S) = √γ(S)`, the leverage-only identity `γ(S) = U(diag P_S)`, the sharp bounds `γ(S) ≥ (n/(n−1))·max_i ℓ_i ≥ p/(n−1)` with its equality case, and the three `n = 4` leverage profiles. Build-inline, in scope, over three dedicated helpers: `Helpers/AffineHull.lean` (`aff(C_n) = c_n P_H + L` where `L = {B symmetric : diag B = 0, B 1 = 0}`, via the four-index alternating-sum identity `q_ik − q_jk − q_iℓ + q_jℓ = 0`, plus `c_n P_H ∈ relint C_n`); `Helpers/GramDiagonal.lean` (prescribed nonnegative diagonal `d` with `D ⪰ 0`, `D 1 = 0` is realizable ⟺ `2 max_i √d_i ≤ ∑_i √d_i`, via the planar-resultant interval `[max(0, 2max r − ∑r), ∑r]` by induction, then a Gram representation); `Helpers/LeverageProfile.lean` (`U(ℓ)` as a one-dimensional feasibility minimum, closedness, upward persistence, bisection validity). SEARCH TRACE for the Gram/polygon fact — `lean_local_search` on `gramMatrix`, `polygonInequality`, `prescribedDiagonal`, `sumZeroVectors`: 0 hits in Causalean; Mathlib-side `lean_leansearch "vectors with prescribed norms summing to zero exist polygon inequality"` returns only triangle-inequality/`SameRay` equality-case lemmas (`not_sameRay_iff_norm_add_lt`, `norm_add_eq_add_norm_iff_angle_eq_zero`) — the EXISTENCE direction is absent. Not found; build-inline (medium, one file), the core's induction supplying the whole argument.

prop:endpoint-reductions.notes: The endpoint/worked-example proposition: `S = H_n` and `S_out` are inadmissible with `v* = c_n`; the `n = 4` intermediate space `S_mid` has `κ = 2/3`, `γ = 8/9`, `ρ* = 2√2/3`; the equal-leverage `S_4 = S_pair` has `v*(ρ) = min{4/3, 2(1−ρ²)}`, `κ = 0`, `γ = 1/3`, `ρ* = 1/√3`; plus the `n = 8`, `M = 1`, `ρ = 1` check `V* = 0 < 4/7 = V_CRD`. Note the core maps a `prop:` node to `lean_kind:"theorem"` (there is no `"proposition"` kind). Build-inline, in scope: the `n = 4` content is finite enumeration of the three balanced sign-pairs in the orthonormal basis `e_j = z^(j)/2`, factored into `Helpers/FourUnit.lean` (with `decide`/`norm_num` on the explicit `4 × 4` matrices); the general-`n` parts reuse `thm:admissibility-frontier` and `lem:pair-space-exact-frontier`. This node also carries the paper's own falsification check (matched pairs are NOT globally dominant), so the encoding must state the exact `v*` branch formula, not merely an inequality.

thm:finite-unknown-quality-regret.notes: The exact finite robust-SDP representation of `R*(n,S)`, outer attainment, the universal bracket `(p/(n−1))(c_n − κ(S)) ≤ (n/4M)R* ≤ c_n − κ(S)` with CRD witnessing the upper bound and homogeneous even blocks attaining the lower bound, and the design-level regret statement over all of `D_n`. Build-inline, in scope. Sub-pieces: the sup-over-shells reduction (core eq. (1)) needs monotonicity of `v` and the score-energy reparametrisation `t = s + (1−s)e`, factored into `Helpers/RegretRepresentation.lean`; joint continuity of `(A,s) ↦ q_s(A)` and hence of `Δ_reg` (compactness ⇒ outer minimizer exists) goes in `Helpers/Compactness.lean`; the trace inequality `n ≤ pK + (n−1−p)L` is one line over `Helpers/Spectral.lean`. The statement must record that `m = C(n, n/2)/2` is generally EXPONENTIAL — a size remark, not a complexity claim (PD-5): no decidability or polynomial-time assertion is encoded.

lem:pair-space-exact-frontier.notes: The partition workhorse: the exact orbit reduction `v*(ρ;S_P) = min_{G ∈ G_P} q_ρ(A_P(G);S_P)`, the parity classification `κ(S_P) = 0 ⟺ every block size is even`, the unequal two-block closed forms (`κ₂`, `b₀`, `s₀`, the `v*` branch formula, the regret `s₀(c_n − κ₂)` and its mixture), the `m = 1` degenerate case, and the homogeneous even-block family (`γ = β`, `R* = 4Mp/(n−1)²`) with matched pairs as the `m = 2` specialization. Build-inline and in scope, but the largest node: split into `Helpers/OrbitReduction.lean` (Jensen over the within-block permutation group; the conditional second moments `E[z_i z_{i'} | r] = r_j r_ℓ/(m_j m_ℓ)` and `(r_j² − m_j)/(m_j(m_j−1))`, i.e. the entries of `A_P(rrᵀ)`; the realizing law = choose signs with the given block sums, permute uniformly within blocks, multiply by an independent fair global sign — `Causalean...prodDesign` / `E_prod_prod` supply the independent-coin layer), `Helpers/BlockSpectrum.lean` (the eigenvalues `a(q) = nq/(mℓ)`, `b_j(q) = (j² − q)/(j(j−1))`, their crossing at `q_c = mℓ/(n−1)`, and the slope sign change at `s₀`), and `Helpers/HomogeneousBlocks.lean` (block-permutation averaging to `aP_S + b(P_H − P_S)`, `pa + hb = n`, the two attaining designs, and the `β`-mixture regret). ANALOGOUS modules: `EXP_DesignPm1ExactnessBoundaryV1_Research/Helpers/{SymmetryReduction,SymRedMatrix,ParitySliceParity,ParitySliceVertices}.lean` — same orbit-averaging and parity-obstruction technique on the two-block index, to be adapted to a general `B`-block labelling.

thm:exact-pair-space-regret.notes: The matched-pair corollary: `v*(ρ;S_pair) = min{c_n, 2(1−ρ²)}`, `κ = 0`, `γ = ρ*² = α_n = (n−2)/(2(n−1))`, the mixture covariance `A_mix = α_n c_n P_H + (1−α_n)·2(P_H − P_S) ∈ C_n`, the exact regret `n(n−2)/(2(n−1)²)` and `R* = 2M(n−2)/(n−1)²`, both endpoint constraints binding, and the `n = 4` sign-pair weights `(1/9, 4/9, 4/9)`. The core itself flags this as a convenience corollary of the homogeneous even-block half of `lem:pair-space-exact-frontier` at `B = n/2`, `m = 2`, so the Lean proof is a specialization plus arithmetic — small, in scope. `Causalean...matchedPairDesign` is the within-pair-orientation design (`A_W = 2 P_T`); it is on the per-pair carrier `P → Bool`, so it enters as a proof template rather than a literal reuse (see the substrate survey).

helpers.content: `lambdaMaxOn` API: Rayleigh sup on a subspace, monotonicity, `λ_max ≥ tr/dim`, `A ⪯ λ P_L`, `P_S A P_S` compression, `max_{X ∈ E_H} tr((A+ηP_S)X) = λ_max(A+ηP_S | H_n)`.

Attainment: the score-constrained unit sphere in `H_n` is compact and the quadratic form continuous, so `shellLoss` is a max; `C_n` is compact (convex hull of a finite set) so `oracleValue` is a min; joint continuity of `(A,s) ↦ q_s(A)` and continuity of `Δ_reg`.

Core eq. (1): every `A ∈ C_n` is PSD, annihilates `1_n`, has unit diagonal and `tr(A | H_n) = n`; hence `λ_max(A | H_n) ≥ c_n` with equality at `A_CRD`. Adapted from `DesignPm1/Helpers/SymRedDesign.lean`.

The elementary compact bilinear minimax on `E_H × [0,K]` and the `ℝ_+^J` projection/separation lemma, both from finite-dimensional strong separation. Mathlib has no convexity-based minimax (search trace in S2), so this is a new, reusable, build-inline helper.
Extreme points of `K_s = X_ρ(S)` are rank one (trace-zero/score-trace-zero perturbation on `range X`), over `Mathlib.Analysis.Convex.{Extreme,KreinMilman}`.
The `Δ_J × K` minimax (core eq. (1) of `thm:exact-oracle-saddle`) and the extraction of optimal sign-pair weights.
`aff(C_n) = c_n P_H + L`, the four-index alternating-sum identity, and `c_n P_H ∈ relint C_n`.

Zero-sum vectors with prescribed norms exist iff `2 max r ≤ ∑ r` (planar resultant interval by induction), hence the Gram characterization of `D ⪰ 0`, `D 1 = 0`, `diag D = d`. Absent from Mathlib (search trace on `thm:admissibility-frontier`).
`U(ℓ)` as a one-dimensional feasibility minimum: closedness, nonemptiness at `t = 1`, upward persistence, attainment.
Within-block permutation orbit averaging (Jensen), the conditional second-moment entries of `A_P(rrᵀ)`, and the realizing balanced law. Adapted from `DesignPm1/Helpers/SymmetryReduction.lean`.
Two-block eigenvalues `a(q)`, `b_j(q)`, their crossing at `q_c`, and the slope sign change at `s₀`.
Block-permutation averaging to `aP_S + b(P_H − P_S)` with `pa + hb = n`; the two attaining designs and the `β`-mixture regret.
The sup-over-shells reduction, monotonicity of `v`, and the robust-SDP epigraph form.
The `n = 4` enumeration: three balanced sign-pairs, the orthonormal basis `e_j = z^(j)/2`, diagonalization of every `A ∈ C_4`, and the three leverage profiles with values `1/3`, `8/9`, `1`.
